Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad followed by one. To withdraw your question, press star two. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jordan Lee, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Mike Patel, CTO; Taylor Kim, Chief Revenue Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Product Officer; and Raj Singh, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially due to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for the third quarter of fiscal 2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our CloudForge AI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on seven key areas: accelerating next quarter ARR growth, optimizing our operating expense breakdown, advancing our product roadmap, raising full-year revenue guidance, strengthening NRR performance, evolving our customer mix, and refining our capital allocation strategy.

These efforts have positioned us for sustained momentum. We are confident in our ability to continue this trajectory and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss the financials in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. As Jordan mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $218 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82%, and operating income was $56 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong at over $2.8 billion, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

Let me start with our outlook for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2024, ending December 31st, and share some context on the key drivers. Our guidance reflects current market conditions, solid visibility into the sales pipeline, and robust momentum across our core segments.

For Q4, we are guiding to ending ARR of $482 million to $488 million, implying sequential quarterly growth of 7% to 8% from our Q3 ending ARR of $451 million. Year-over-year, this equates to 29% to 31% growth, surpassing our full-year target of 27% ARR growth and setting us up for another record year. This would be our 14th straight quarter of at least 25% YoY ARR growth, highlighting the resilience of our land-and-expand approach even with high interest rates and longer sales cycles for big deals.

Breaking it down, customer expansion is central. We anticipate dollar-based net retention, or DBNER, at 115% to 117% for the quarter, in line with Q3's 116%. This comes from cohort expansions and AI-driven upsells. CloudForge AI, our generative AI suite from Q2, boasts a 42% attach rate among exposed customers, akin to Slack's AI workflows or Zoom's tools, embedding into operations with $28K average ACV uplift per seat. We closed over 150 AI-related expansions in Q3 and expect 200-plus in Q4, especially from enterprises where NRR exceeds 120%.

New logo wins are gaining steam too, with $32 million to $35 million in new ARR adds, up 12% sequentially. Roughly 60% from net new customers at $145K average ACV, favoring quicker mid-market deals under $250K. Our freemium-to-enterprise funnel, like Notion's growth strategy, boosted qualified opportunities 28% quarter-over-quarter from self-serve. Sales cycles hold at 65 days for sub-$100K ACV deals, edging to 95 days for $1M-plus due to procurement, but no major issues.

Geographically balanced: North America at 68% of ARR grows 8% sequentially, powered by a $15M federal agency deal and financial services gains displacing old SharePoint systems. EMEA, 22% of ARR, accelerates 9-10% sequentially via GDPR-ready AI and AWS co-sells into 40 new logos. APAC at 10% eyes 6% growth despite yen and China challenges, offset by Japan and India successes like an $8M telco expansion, echoing Atlassian's plays.

Technically, Q3 updates like zero-ETL with Snowflake and Databricks lift win rates 15 points over monday.com. GTM targets healthcare via FHIR modules for $2B TAM and agentic AI copilots automating 30% of tasks, like Adobe Firefly gains. Gross dollar churn stays under 1%, with 98% multi-year renewals at 62% of new ARR.

Risks include macro capex freezes, FX shaving 50-75 bps, and competition from Snowflake's tools. Still, our flywheel—sticky adoption, AI expansions, execution—positions us for industry 18% growth per Gartner, lapping FY2024 and aiming $600M-plus ARR run-rate into FY2025.

Next, on operating expenses. Total op ex hit $162 million, up 18% YoY but flat QoQ, at 74% of revenue versus 82% last year, delivering operating leverage and a Rule of 40 score of 62 from 35% growth and 27% adjusted EBITDA margins.

R&D at $68 million or 31% of revenue, down 200 bps YoY. Up 15% from $59 million, but efficiency shines. Investments ramp in gen AI and agentic workflows post-ForgeAI launch, lifting NRR 150 bps to 118%. Engineering headcount up 12% to 450-plus for real-time multimodal synthesis and zero-trust with FedRAMP High, GDPR 2.0—like Snowflake Cortex or Databricks MosaicML. 60% US in Seattle/Austin, doubled Bangalore to 120 for infra like Kubernetes, boosting output 18% via deployments, MTTR. Targeting 28-30% through FY2025 for AI agents automating 40% workflows, like Salesforce Agentforce, with 25% ACV uplift in Fortune 1000 pilots.

Sales & Marketing at $62 million or 28% of revenue, down 500 bps YoY, up 12% YoY but down 5% QoQ. CAC payback to 14 months from 18, LTV/CAC 4.2x. Shift to enterprise: paid media/events 25%, AI intent from 6sense cuts CAC 22% mid-market. Sales to 320 reps, up 8%, enterprise focus; cut field marketing 10% for ABM in finance/healthcare, 15 $1M-plus deals. EMEA 22% bookings up from 15%, 30 sales in London/Dublin; APAC 8% via Tencent. Ahead, 25-27%, freemium like HubSpot, 65% attach on ForgeSecurity.

G&A $32 million or 15% flat YoY, up 8%. SBC $12M or 38%, down slightly post stock rise. Fees for SOC 2, IFRS leases; headcount flat 180, legal/compliance for expansion. Remote saves 20% facilities. APAC up 15% compliance.

Overall, opex scales well: FY2024 at 72%, leverage to FY2025 with 122% NRR, $1B ARR path.

Turning to full-year FY2024 revenue guidance. Year-to-date $435 million implied strong, ahead plan. Raising to $565 million to $585 million, 32% to 37% YoY growth from prior $540-565M. Midpoint $575M caps 11 years 30%+ ARR growth.

New logos $180-190M new ARR, up from $170M prior. CloudForge AI in CI/CD like GitHub Copilot speeds deploys 40%, ACVs to $450K enterprise, serverless for edge/K8s. Expansions $140-150M at 118% NRR, security SOC2/FedRAMP like Datadog. Flexible pricing +3pts expansion.

US 65% $370-380M +35%; EMEA $105-110M +30% GDPR/UK auto; APAC 15% $65-70M +45% Tokyo/AWS Japan, India/Brazil channels; FX -1-2pts.

Investing AI DevOps, Q3 ForgeML agentic like Harness. $75M SecuraFlow buy lifts LTV/CAC 4.2x. Rule 50 at 58%. Risks: recession SMB churn 8%, comp Atlassian, cycles; conservative $10M, margins 22-24%.

On NRR, Q3 dollar-based 118%, 11th quarter over 110%, +400bps YoY from 114%, elite vs Snowflake 128%, SaaS median 105-110% Bessemer.

Gross retention 96%, multi-year, high switch costs for 5K+ customers incl Fortune 500 banks, ServiceNow-like.

Expansion 28% net: $15M from ForgeAI Insights gen AI predictive like Slack/Anthropic, 42% adopt >$100K ARR, 25% per cust; usage seats +18% SMB; cross-sell security 65 deals $8M +30% QoQ. NA 32% AWS/Azure, EMEA 22% certs.

Contraction 6% stable <7% target, mid-market headcount adjusts like Zoom, churn predict models; pricing 2%.

Churn 4% logo/3% revenue, lowest, 0 top 100 losses. 78% rev 3+ modules vs 62% YoY. APAC 6% yen/local comp, addressing hires/J-SOX.

NRR validates platform: Q4 ForgeAI $50M+ expansion, 120%+ target, CS AI agents <5% contraction FY25. $450M+ ARR year-end vs macro.

Customer mix: Enterprise >$100K ACV 48% ARR up from 42% YoY/45% Q2; SMB <$100K 52% from 58%. Enterprise net adds 32 +28% YoY to 285; SMB 1,800 +12% to 14,500+. Ent ACV $285K +15%, SMB $28K.

Enterprise DBNRR 128% peak, 65% expand 12mo AI Agent/Zero-Trust FedRAMP. SMB 112%, churn 8% from 7% macro hiring.

NA 62% ARR ent 55% Fortune CPG; EMEA 22% ent up 16% GDPR/SAP; APAC 16% SMB 72% but ent pilots +40% fin serv Temenos; LatAm 4-5% SMB.

Design: post K8s re-arch sub-50ms, Ent Success shortens cycles 9-6mo >$500K; SMB $49/mo starter Zapier-like. FY25 ent 52-55%, $2.1B pipe 60% ent, 3.2yr contracts. De-risks: ent stability 2x margins, SMB 70% NRR viral vs Monday/Workday.

Capital allocation: Balance sheet $2.8B cash, $1.9B net post $900M notes. FCF $450M +28% YoY, flexibility.

Prioritize TAM/moat/growth, >25% ROIC vs ServiceNow/Snowflake. 65% FY24 capex/OCF $1.2B organic R&D/GTM. R&D 22% rev +3pts AI suite $300M multimodal CRM/collab like Agentforce/Firefly, upsell +45% QoQ 15% new ACV. GTM verticals healthcare/finserv NRR 118%>110%. APAC 18% bookings +6pts $150M Japan/India.

M&A 20% $450M three deals. $280M DataForge Q2 95% margins $60M ARR Snowflake-like data pipes, cross-sell +30% 20% new logos. SecureVault/FlowOptix 3x ROI 18mo like Workday/HubSpot. Pipeline 5-7 $100-500M AI/EMEA, up to $1B '25 at 8-10x ARR.

Shareholder returns: $250M buyback avg $145 2% float, $2B auth 60% left, +4-5% EPS accretive P/E 32x vs 45x SaaS. No div growth focus, pause large amid Treasuries.

Leverage 0.8x, $3.5B credit. Stress 10% downside 24+ mo runway. Capex <3% AWS AI.

Deployed since '22 35% ARR CAGR 50% FCF, acquired 22% ARR +40%.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance, now expecting revenue in the range of $565 million to $585 million.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel for a technology update.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability, including zero-trust primitives with Confidential Computing on AWS Nitro Enclaves and Kubernetes-native multi-tenancy, to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers achieving 99.999% uptime SLA.

And now Elena Vasquez will provide an update on the product roadmap.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Mike. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited about tremendous momentum across the CloudForge Analytics platform, delivering composable AI-native analytics at enterprise scale for real-time insights from petabyte datasets for Fortune 500 retailers and banks.

Recent launches: Q1 ForgeAI Insights gen AI copilot with OpenAI APIs for natural language on SQL/docs/IoT video. 42% paying customers active, +28% MAU/account, 3x faster TTV vs Snowflake Cortex, query times 15min to 2min, 15% analyst reduction at European bank beta.

Late Q2 Unified Marketplace 2.0, 300+ connectors Salesforce Einstein/HubSpot/ServiceNow, NRR to 118% from 112%, 2.5x ACV core to data ops $450K.

Upcoming: Agentic AI ForgeAI Agents GA next qtr, end-to-end workflows anomaly detect/remediate ERP, mixture-of-experts on 10T+ tokens vs ThoughtSpot/Sigma. Multimodal vision-language dashboards/exec summaries.

EdgeForge serverless edge runtime for 5G/hybrid, low-latency manuf/telcos, 60% less egress vs BigQuery, pilots three top telcos sub-50ms.

Tech: Composable arch v5.2 85% migrated, infinite scale eBPF pipes. Security zero-trust SOC2 all regions.

Adoption: Q3 35% YoY ARR new modules, AI $28M +15% target. Churn <5% multi-module vs 8-10% ind. Data vol +52%, consumption 40% bookings.

Regions: NA 62%, EMEA +48% GDPR DAX40, APAC +62% Singapore/Tokyo sovereign, LatAm 5% $12M Brazil fintech Spanish/Portuguese NLP.

Strategic: Outbound innovation 125% NRR AI adopters vs Bessemer 10-15% logo slowdown. 28% R&D $145M FY, 30%+ FY25 growth. Embed as AI data layer like Confluent streaming/dbt transforms. Margin to 32% EBITDA year-end.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Elena. This quarter our focus was on increasing our brand awareness and lead generation through targeted digital campaigns and strategic partnerships. We saw a 25% increase in website traffic and a 35% increase in qualified leads, demonstrating the effectiveness of our marketing initiatives, including AI-driven intent tools and ABM in key verticals.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question at this time, please press star one on your telephone keypad followed by one. Our first question comes from Ben Thompson with Morningstar.

Ben Thompson:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of CloudForge AI on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, how it compares to your initial expectations, and what's the competitive landscape like?

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Ben. CloudForge AI has been transformative for growth, contributing over $28 million in incremental ARR this quarter alone through expansions and new logos. Attach rates are at 42% among eligible customers, driving $28K ACV uplift per seat and 25% average expansion per account. This is well ahead of our initial expectations, where we modeled 30% adoption; we've exceeded by 40% due to faster embedding in workflows. Competitively, it differentiates us sharply—our zero-ETL integrations and agentic capabilities outpace monday.com and ThoughtSpot in head-to-heads, with 15-point win rate lifts, while mirroring but surpassing Snowflake Cortex in analytics depth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, what are your key target markets, and what are your expected ROI from these investments?

Jordan Lee:
Great question, Lisa. International expansion is a priority, with APAC as a high-conviction area guiding to 6% sequential growth despite headwinds. Plans include ramping sales teams in Tokyo and Singapore, launching localized data centers, and deepening hyperscaler partnerships like AWS Japan and Tencent. Key targets are Japan telcos and India fintechs, plus Australia financial services—recent $8M telco win exemplifies. We expect ROI of 3x within 18 months on $150 million invested, based on 45% YoY APAC revenue growth YTD and pilots converting at 65% velocity, aligning with Atlassian-like regional scaling.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Park with Barclays.

David Park:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, what are your strategies to improve customer retention, and what's the impact of pricing changes on churn?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, David. Churn management emphasizes proactive success teams and AI prediction models, keeping gross dollar churn under 1% and logo churn at 4%—lowest ever, zero in top 100. NRR trends strong at 118% Q3, up 400bps YoY, targeting 120%+ Q4 driven by 28% expansions offsetting 6% contraction. Retention strategies include dedicated TAMs for enterprise, multi-year contracts at 62% new ARR (98% renewals), CS AI agents for upsells, and vertical playbooks shortening cycles. Pricing changes—flexible seat-based and annual true-ups—have neutral to positive impact, adding just 2% leakage while boosting expansions 3 points QoQ.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Jordan Lee for closing remarks.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
